sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: A student project exploring a wearable lower-limb exoskeleton, based initially on the open-source OpenExo platform.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: Explore ways to support movement while addressing comfort, weight, power use and coordination with the wearer.

sections.heading: Our approach
sections.body: The initial technical focus is the hip joint. The project combines mechanical design, electronics and automation; possible future control approaches include movement sensing and muscle signals.

sections.heading: Current stage and progress
sections.body: The project is listed as execution in progress. Assembly and testing progress needs confirmation.

sections.heading: Roadmap
sections.body: The existing plan describes obtaining and manufacturing parts, assembling a hip prototype and considering further development after the initial build.

sections.heading: Expected outcomes and impact
sections.body: A hip exoskeleton prototype and practical experience in robotics, electronics and control.

sections.heading: Team and partners
sections.body: The project documentation describes a collaboration between BEA and AEA, with mechanics, electronics and automation teams. Named participants need confirmation.

sections.heading: Resources and collaboration
sections.body: The project uses the open-source OpenExo resources. Current funding and support needs: -

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: A student-led wearable project exploring how to monitor physiological signals and support personal insights while considering user privacy.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: Bring together multiple sensing and data-processing functions in a compact wearable system.

sections.heading: Our approach
sections.body: The proposed system combines sensors for heart rate and oxygenation, movement, skin temperature and skin conductance, with software for analysis. Local data processing is part of the project concept.

sections.heading: Current stage and progress
sections.body: The project is listed as execution in progress. Prototype and validation status need confirmation.

sections.heading: Roadmap
sections.body: The documented direction includes integrating components into a miniaturised printed circuit board and developing the associated software.

sections.heading: Expected outcomes and impact
sections.body: A wearable prototype and an integrated approach to collecting and interpreting physiological data.

sections.heading: Team and partners
sections.body: The documentation describes hardware, firmware and software work across a multidisciplinary team. Named members: -

sections.heading: Resources and collaboration

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: Help students understand the journey from a digital model to a printable physical object.

sections.heading: Our approach
sections.body: The proposed programme covers printing technologies, materials, modelling, printability, slicing, printer use and analysis of printed results. Group activities apply these skills to a design challenge.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: An introductory course concept exploring brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) through practical work on motor imagery.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: Help students learn how to acquire and process brain-signal data and explore BCI applications.

sections.heading: Our approach
sections.body: The proposed course combines teaching, practical exercises and a project using an EMOTIV device, with Python as a foundation.

sections.heading: Current stage and progress
sections.body: The course is listed as execution in progress. The available detailed plan is preliminary and needs an update.

sections.heading: Roadmap
sections.body: The initial plan proposes preparing teaching material, testing the acquisition and processing pipeline, and delivering guided practical sessions.

sections.heading: Expected outcomes and impact

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: A research project exploring a microfluidic device concept for therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) of vancomycin and gentamicin.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: The project examines whether a small sample could support the monitoring of two antibiotics through a single integrated workflow.

sections.heading: Our approach
sections.body: The proposed chip would separate plasma and divide the sample into two channels, exploring electrochemical detection for vancomycin and optical detection for gentamicin. These are concepts to investigate.

sections.heading: Current stage and progress
sections.body: The project is listed as execution in progress. The available project document describes a concept and simulation phase; current results need confirmation.

sections.heading: Roadmap
sections.body: The documented plan includes literature and patent research, chip design, flow and diffusion simulations, assessment of detection methods and a final report.

sections.heading: Expected outcomes and impact
sections.body: Planned outputs include a CAD concept, simulation results, a comparison with existing approaches and a development roadmap.

sections.heading: Team and partners
sections.body: The proposed roles cover project management, literature and patent research, CAD and simulation, detection methods, and documentation. Current named members: -

sections.heading: Resources and collaboration
sections.body: The plan mentions CAD tools and COMSOL Multiphysics. Confirmed budget and collaboration needs: -

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: A BEA and PMDS project developing a wearable concept for an inner-speech interface.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: Explore alternative ways for people with speech difficulties to communicate.

sections.heading: Our approach
sections.body: The team is exploring a wearable device that captures signals and micro-movements associated with the intention to speak, with the aim of decoding them into text or voice commands.

sections.heading: Current stage and progress
sections.body: An October 2026 presentation reports an initial prototype, data collection and tests of model training. The latest results need confirmation.

sections.heading: Roadmap
sections.body: The presentation describes testing additional sensors and improving the approach towards an advanced prototype. Current milestones: -

sections.heading: Expected outcomes and impact
sections.body: A more advanced prototype and a better understanding of the sensing and machine-learning pipeline.

sections.heading: Team and partners
sections.body: The project is presented as a collaboration between BEA and PMDS, bringing together hardware, software and product-design skills. Named members: -
